key_insight: A non-local three-wave-mixing model can look integrable in global level statistics while still thermalizing dynamically because kinematic constraints fragment Hilbert space into ergodic sectors.
engineering_relevance: The result identifies a measurable bottleneck mechanism in superconducting cavity–qubit platforms that can affect how fast quantum signals spread and how reliably such systems reach equilibrium.
method: Exact diagonalization of the three-wave-mixing Hamiltonian
Comparison of spectral statistics, inverse participation ratios, and entanglement entropy
Time-domain diagnostics using dynamics and OTOCs
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that global level-spacing statistics appear integrable, while inverse participation ratios, entanglement fluctuations, and OTOCs all indicate ergodicity, rapid scrambling within sectors, and logarithmically slow relaxation overall.
watch_item: Because the behavior is driven by strong Hilbert-space fragmentation and finite-size exact diagonalization, larger devices may show size-dependent crossover effects that complicate direct experimental interpretation.
paper_title: Unconventional Thermalization of a Three-Wave-Mixing Model
